highlights.title: Chelsea in landmark fertility policy: 'Being a player and mum are both possible now'
highlights.summary: Chelsea are used to being the first. While plenty of that has come on the pitch, it is the behind the scenes work that is truly leading the way for female players and women's health.
body: Now, the Blues are the first team in the WSL to introduced new fertility and maternity policies, giving their players the choice to start a family in whichever way they want to, and the post-natal support to balance the demands of elite sport and motherhood.

The Blues were also the first club in the world to starting tracking menstrual cycles - introduced by Emma Hayes in February 2020 - and how they impact performance. This is the next step in that process.

Chelsea have partnered with Fertility Plus - one of London's leading fertility clinics - to set up a fund accessible to all players in support of their fertility journey. This includes egg freezing, IVF, smear tests and contraception, as well as counselling and workshops to give players everything they need to make informed choices It is not an enforced policy and players can access it however they need with support from Chelsea.

body: This means Mo.co will run “on low maintenance,” says Supercell, and no further weapons or premium tracks will be released. Elite merch and content “will be recycled from previous seasons.”

“Our goal is to release updates more frequently and reduce the wait between them,” the team explained, adding there was no date planned for the next update, but it expected to roll one out before the end of 2026.

highlights.title: ‘Florid’ Director Billy Lumby on Challenging ‘Misrepresentation’ of Schizophrenia on Screen and Casting Non-Actors in Feature Debut
highlights.summary: The depiction of schizophrenia on screen — especially in horror movies — has largely seen the mental health condition linked to violent and unpredictable rages, showing people when something has gone horribly wrong.
body: While the story doesn’t culminate in the violent depths seen in the cinema tropes Lumby was purposefully looking to avoid, it’s a tough watch. But that’s largely due to the aural sensation provided by the voices, which become more powerful and prominent as the film progresses, dragging Jamal down with them.

Carrying “Florid” as Jamal is Jonathan Jules, best known for Steve McQueen’s “Small Axe,” in his first lead role. “It’s not easy to act in a mentally unwell state in an authentic, accurate way,” notes Lumby.

During filming, Jules wore earpieces on set, with actors in another room speaking into microphones so he could hear the voices live and respond in an unrestricted way. “There were theses little moments where his eyes twitched — it just made if feel so real,” says Lumby. After principal photography wrapped, many months would be spent in post-production augmenting the voices to create the right tone and weave them into the overall soundscape.

highlights.title: Estimating suicide risk from text
highlights.summary: A new language-processing tool could help identify the highest-risk individuals from natural language, enabling swifter interventions.
body: When people reach out during a mental health crisis, a top priority for counselors is identifying those with a high risk of suicide. The distressed person’s language holds critical clues, and a new tool developed by scientists at MIT’s McGovern Institute for Brain Research is designed to pick up on and rapidly evaluate those signals.

The language-processing tool was developed by Daniel Low, a former graduate student in Senior Research Scientist Satra Ghosh ’s Senseable Intelligence Group who is now a research scientist at the Child Mind Institute, where he leads its AI, Risk, and Contemplative Science Lab, as well as a visiting scholar at Harvard University. It uses a custom-built list of words and phrases linked to 49 suicide risk factors, searching text for these and using them to estimate an individual’s risk.

highlights.title: 'Exploitative ideas' - Top leagues criticise Infantino and call for FIFA reform
highlights.summary: A joint statement from Europe's top leagues has hit out at "exploitative ideas" pushed by FIFA president Gianni Infantino and called for "essential" reform of football's governing body.
body: This summer, Infantino was forced to abandon a plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup after a backlash which led to UEFA pursuing legal action.

Earlier this week, in a letter to FIFA members, Infantino said he was open to an independent external review of the plan and that he should be allowed to continue leading FIFA because his responsibilities are "larger than any individual proposal or disagreement". There will be a FIFA presidential election in March 2027.

However, the Premier League, Bundesliga, LaLiga and Serie A chiefs have now called for "a new governance structure for our sport's global governing body that is transparent, objective, proportionate and inclusive".

"Football's longstanding foundations have, in recent years, been threatened by a fundamental governance problem, whereby FIFA's president has actively promoted exploitative ideas rather than safeguarding against them," the leagues say.

highlights.title: PlayStation Wants You to Use Your Controller to Simplify Payments
highlights.summary: Near Field Communication, commonly known as NFC, has simplified card transactions, greatly speeding up the payment process. According to a recently filed patent, Sony wants to bring NFC to its DualSense controllers in order to enable faster PlayStation purchases.
body: Every player who uses a controller knows how much effort it takes to type using the D-pad and analog stick. You have to go through this process when entering passwords or adding card information. Most phones on the market feature NFC, which allows users to hold their device near a payment terminal to complete a transaction. This comes in particularly handy when making everyday purchases, as it eliminates the need to pull out your wallet, insert the card into the machine, and enter your passcode. Sony also wants to simplify the payment process on console by adding NFC to PlayStation controllers.

With this technology, players would be able to complete a purchase simply by holding their phone or card near the DualSense. But that's not all — if you were able to easily connect your phone to the console, it would also open the door for all sorts of data transfers via NFC.

highlights.summary: Expert says Australia’s criminal laws should be clarified to determine how fault is applied to a corporation when its AI agent commits a crime. Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates. Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: The federal government could change Australian laws if the current legal framework could not respond to the unprecedented OpenAI hack of Medicare, ministers have confirmed.

It comes as the prime minister denied accusations from the opposition he had held on to the information before announcing it at the UN general assembly in New York, and said it was released at the first possible opportunity.
“It’s just nonsense … I was informed while I’ve been in New York,” Anthony Albanese told News24 on Friday.

highlights.title: 5 Essential Backrooms Videos to Watch on YouTube After the Movie
highlights.summary: Taken together, the YouTube videos do connect, though not always in particularly useful ways — and they might help you deepen your understanding of the movie. A 30-second clip called 9780415263573, for instance, appears to be highway-camera footage of a car disappearing.
body: Most of Parsons’ YouTube shorts are snippets that elliptically suggest a larger story without actually telling it, and many end in the middle of a scene, before resolving whatever is happening. Unlike traditional found-footage horror, which creators generally style as unearthed video that somehow contains a complete story, Parsons’ uploads truly feel like unanchored digital remnants recovered from a discarded, corrupted hard drive. Watch them all and you can piece together the beginnings of a narrative. In the later videos especially, a few characters persist from one installment to another, and the contours of a larger story start to emerge. But that story still hasn’t been fully told.

Still, if you’re new to the Backrooms phenomenon, loved the movie, and want more — or if you just want the best taste of the online work that inspired boutique studio A24 to pursue Parsons for a feature film — these are the five essential videos from his Backrooms series.

After reporting on artificial intelligence for years, I was curious about what the technology could do for me. I had imagined Cowork as a hyper-capable digital assistant, but was let down to discover that it was more like interacting with a regular chatbot, albeit one with extra tools. What did I want it to do? I had no idea.

Then Instinct, an invite-only AI agent that communicates with users through iMessage and WhatsApp, started popping off in the Bay Area. It connects to your email, calendar, and messaging apps. Think of it as OpenClaw for normies. The company, which launched in private beta in February, is reportedly in talks to raise $1 billion on top of the $350 million it’s already raised, bringing its valuation to $10 billion, according to The Information.

highlights.title: 29 Years Later, Charlie Brown's Wisest Quote Is Still an All-Time 'Peanuts' Classic
highlights.summary: By now, 26 years after the strip ended, Peanuts often feels like it comes pre-digested. Even during its original run, much of Peanuts got carefully filtered through layers of T-shirts, greeting cards, and inspirational wall posters.
body: When you actually read the strip for itself, it can be a surprise to find that Peanuts, particularly in the first half of its run, has more of an edge than it gets credit for. In fact, what put it on the map in the first place was how Charles Schulz depicted childhood. At a point when many other cartoonists focused on the nostalgic joys of being a kid, Schulz wrote about its confusions and quiet terrors.

It's often forgotten now, after decades of enshrinement in the American pop-cultural canon, but this is easily the most subversive element of the strip. Peanuts is frequently a meditation on how rough it really is to be a little kid, which made it a strong counterpoint to the more saccharine vibes of 1950s newspaper gag comics.

Even during its original run, much of Peanuts got carefully filtered through layers of T-shirts, greeting cards, and inspirational wall posters.

Peanuts is frequently a meditation on how rough it really is to be a little kid, which made it a strong counterpoint to the more saccharine vibes of 1950s newspaper gag comics.

highlights.title: From bling and birds to ‘really fancy armour’ – the best dressed characters of the Bayeux tapestry
highlights.summary: Medieval experts talk us through the fashion of the near-1,000-year-old embroidered work, and what it says about the characters wearing it. Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: Blood, booze, arrows and boats; these are what you might typically imagine when you think of the Bayeux tapestry, which has become one of the hottest historical tickets since it went on display at the British Museum in London this month. But what about the hair?

“The Anglo-Saxons all have these little moustaches, which are brilliant. And then the Normans have these funny haircuts with the back of their heads shaved,” says Prof Laura Cleaver, an expert in medieval manuscripts at the Institute of English Studies.
And the clothes? There are crowns and tights, and brooches that wouldn’t look out of place anchoring one of Colman Domingo’s lapels at the Oscars.
The 70-metre-long embroidery – it’s famously not, in fact, a tapestry – was stitched almost 1,000 years ago and tells the story of the Norman conquest.

highlights.title: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone
highlights.summary: Meta has a new plan to get people to make games for its Horizon social platform. The company today announced two new development tools that will let you create games with AI prompts: Horizon Create, a mobile app, and Horizon Studio, a browser app that offers more granular controls.
body: Horizon has struggled as a platform, but Meta has a plan to give these new Horizon games significantly more reach: It’s going to let published games made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio get recommended on Facebook and Instagram, where they also will be playable.

“Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected,” Meta says. “Your game lives natively in the feeds where people already discover content and connect with friends.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will get more reach, according to the company.

The company’s announcement comes as Roblox, a similar platform to Horizon that is vastly more popular, is also making a significant push into AI-powered development, including a feature in its mobile app that similarly allows users to generate games with a prompt.

Meta’s news about Horizon, which launched as a VR app, follows a recent pivot to primarily focus on mobile. With Meta stuffing AI into basically everything it can, it’s perhaps no surprise that AI is becoming a big part of Horizon as well.

highlights.title: 2026’s Most Inventive Sci-Fi Thriller Is Officially Making Its Streaming Debut
highlights.summary: If 2026 has proven anything, it's that horror filmmaking is firing on all cylinders. Earlier in the year, Curry Barker dissected modern intimacy through the nightmare lens of Obsession, while Damian McCarthy built a masterclass in spatial dread and folklore with Hokum.
body: None, however, have topped the liminal nightmare of Kane Parsons’ Backrooms. A film that translated internet mythos into a box-office-shattering theatrical event, it transposes the eerie familiarity of fluorescent-lit architecture into pure terror, and it’s finally streaming on HBO Max starting today, Sept. 25. Whether you missed the film’s big-screen run or simply want to get lost in its endless fluorescent maze again, it remains the essential home-viewing release of the season for horror aficionados.

Chiwetel Ejiofor stars as Clark, a struggling furniture store owner whose life has not gone quite the way he had expected. During an exploration of the basement beneath his store, Clark discovers a strange crack in the wall that leads into a seemingly infinite maze of interconnected spaces. At first, the discovery feels almost like an impossible gift. Clark begins documenting and mapping the space, stealing some of the furniture within while attempting to understand the strange world he stumbled into. But the deeper Clark goes, the clearer it becomes that the Backrooms are not simply an architectural curiosity.

highlights.title: It’s sinister that Meta’s Muse AI mascot is so cute
highlights.summary: This is Optimizer, a weekly newsletter sent from Verge senior reviewer Victoria Song that dissects and discusses the latest gizmos and potions that swear they're going to change your life. Opt in for Optimizer here.
body: Meta wants to stuff this guy into everything and entrust it with productivity, health, and relationship goals.

Last night, I asked Blorbo — what I named my Muse AI agent — to help me set some health goals. I was underwhelmed. I’d asked for a workout regimen for a sub-30 minute 5K and regaining lost muscle. It generated an okay-ish but kind of mid weekly routine.

But then I looked at its face. Based on what it learned about me from my emails, it had morphed into cat-shaped piece of bread with a Kirby-like face. It was so stinking cute, it was like getting zapped with the Men in Black’s neuralizer. Until then, I’d been circumspect about sharing too much about my health. But as that cute face gazed into my soul, I started sharing more to see if my recommendations would improve.

I’ve been aggressively avoiding Muse since it launched a few weeks ago. Sure, some of that is because I was busy testing other devices. But the number-one reason why is that I am horribly vulnerable when faced with extreme cuteness.

body: "We’re seeing a large and growing group of Raiders who come to the Rust Belt for the co-op and the ARC, not fighting with other Raiders," Embark say in the post announcing the trial. "That group has become a core part of our community, so it’s important we learn how to support them properly rather than leave them working around the game."

To back this up, the studio share some data they've collected, showing that there are now more players that play only friendly co-op and never attack other humans than the merciless pure PvP bunch. Apparently the PvP group has remained at a stable 34% since the game's launch, but the number of mixed players, who spend most their time being affable members of the post-apocalypse society but occasionally dabble in wanton homicide, has shrunk, with most opting to become full-time peaceniks.

“This is the same here, and we simply had to make this movie,” added Pösö, who produces with Finland’s No-Office Films, in co-production with Ireland’s Vico Films.

“This story was inspired by my family, and my experience of growing up in Finland, where no one had seen black people!” said Dublin and Helsinki-based Mohamud, who studied filmmaking at London Metropolitan University and USC (University of Southern California) in Los Angeles. highlights.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for Belgian buns | The sweet spot
highlights.summary: These old-school classic treats may struggle for attention among today’s more Instagram-worthy cardamon buns, but they’re simple to make and divine to devour. Belgian buns are among a dying breed of bakes, forgotten about in favour of pretty cinnamon and cardamom buns and creative laminated doughs.
body: Put the flour, sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl or stand mixer, and mix briefly to combine. pour in the milk, water, one egg, and the lemon zest, and stir until the mixture comes together into a shaggy dough. Knead by hand for eight to 10 minutes (or in a stand mixer for about five minutes), until you have a soft dough, then leave to rest uncovered for five minutes.

Pat the dough flat on a lightly floured work surface and smush the butter all over the top. Fold the dough over itself, then knead again; it’s a messy job, but use a dough scraper to scrape the surface often and it will eventually all come together. Once the butter is completely incorporated and the dough looks silky and shiny, put it in a lightly greased bowl, cover and leave to prove in a warm place for two to three hours, until puffy and nearly doubled in size.

Knock the air out of the dough, then tip it out on to a lightly floured work surface. Roll it out to a roughly 35cm x 25cm rectangle, then spoon the lemon curd on top and spread it out evenly. Sprinkle the sultanas all over.
points: These old-school classic treats may struggle for attention among today’s more Instagram-worthy cardamon buns, but they’re simple to make and divine to devour.
